### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 898c2f469b69fba42d7e4e99b161ddc7fcdc63f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd7070d3bf2aca28d4e3add1714051d9dea5eb46` — the merge of head `007510f8a4ac950bc019921fd7e49831e7558940` into base `898c2f469b69fba42d7e4e99b161ddc7fcdc63f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd7070d3bf2aca28d4e3add1714051d9dea5eb46 && git checkout dd7070d3bf2aca28d4e3add1714051d9dea5eb46
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 898c2f469b69fba42d7e4e99b161ddc7fcdc63f9 007510f8a4ac950bc019921fd7e49831e7558940 && git checkout -B drift-repro 898c2f469b69fba42d7e4e99b161ddc7fcdc63f9 && git merge --no-ff 007510f8a4ac950bc019921fd7e49831e7558940

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 898c2f469b69fba42d7e4e99b161ddc7fcdc63f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80e82e18a14993f97e26900cf4a7b7289ae2e444`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-flow-clone-custom-package.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-flow-door-package-address.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/meta-managed-content-seal.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/meta-overlay-read-your-writes.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts + (read, not reviewed) packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md; the changeset is judged in ② only

**Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-10T20:35Z. They had NOT all concluded, and in-progress is not green.**
- Concluded `success`: Check Changeset, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter.
- `in_progress`, no conclusion: Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI.
- No check-run had concluded red. The rest were `skipped`.
- This verdict is of the contract (① to ④). It does not stand in for the runs above: the PR lands only once they conclude green, and a red there is not covered by this record. The PR is still a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The rule matches the engine's start-node check exactly. Right.** The engine: `validateStartNode`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts` L292-293, returns no refusal when `flow.nodes.some(...)` finds a node whose `type === 'start'`. The lint: `scanStartNodeMissing` returns when `nodes.some(...)` finds a node whose `type === START_NODE_TYPE`, over the flow's top-level `nodes`.
   - Zero start nodes: both refuse. An empty list: both refuse.
   - More than one: neither refuses (the engine runs from the first, `engine.ts` L7205 `flow.nodes.find`), and `flow-node-unreachable` names the extra one. Pinned by a control case.
   - A start node only in a region body: both read the top-level list only, so both refuse. Pinned.
   - A different spelling (`Start`, `START`): `FlowNodeSchema.type` is an open string with no normalisation, and both compare with `===`, so both refuse. No D2 conversion entry rewrites a node type to or from `start` (the ten `flow-*` entries under `packages/spec/src/conversions/entries` touch config keys, the retired callout names and decision mode).
   - Status: the engine check is status-agnostic (an `obsolete` or `draft`-status flow is checked too), and the lint reads no status. Equal.
   - Body judged: the save door hands the gate the D2-converted body and the engine sees the parsed flow; neither step adds or removes a node. A non-list `nodes` is refused by `FlowSchema` (`nodes: z.array(...)`, required) before either.
   - I could construct no flow the engine refuses on this check and lint passes, and none the reverse.
2. **The start literal is read from the spec. Right.** `START_NODE_TYPE = FlowNodeAction.enum.start`. The engine restates `'start'`; that file is outside the diff.
3. **Accept-set narrowing at three places. Right, and declared.** `os lint` / `os build` / `os validate` (the registry entry is `tier: 'gating'`, `commands: ALL`); the live save (`protocol-save.ts` L1688, `state: 'active'` unless `mode: 'draft'`); the per-item and package publish (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts` L969). A draft save reaches `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` with `state: 'draft'` and gets advisories only, and its read takes the publish verdict into `_diagnostics` through `draftPublishVerdict`.
4. **Public surface widened. Right, and declared.** `FLOW_START_NODE_MISSING` is exported from `@objectstack/lint` and `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` gains one entry. No registry entry is added, so no rule count moves.
5. **No `FlowSchema` refinement and nothing under `packages/spec/src`. Right**, as the card asks.
6. **An already-stored live flow with no start node stays fixable and retirable. Right.** The gate has no stored-row baseline, so a live re-save that leaves the flow start-less is refused, whatever else it edits (a `status: 'obsolete'` re-save included). The save that adds a start node passes. A draft save passes. Delete carries no body and runs no gate. `source: 'migrate-stored'` and the `package-author` channel return clean before the rules run. The automation door (`POST` / `PUT /api/v1/automation`) registers with the engine before it saves, so #32273 already refused there. The toggle writes an activation row, not the body. Nothing is locked in.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right spelling; the claim's `no (narrowing)` was an expectation.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines `yes (narrowing)` as a diff that widens one surface and narrows another, and `no (narrowing)` as not a widening but breaking. This diff does both: it narrows the accept set and adds a public export. CONTRIBUTING item 5 says `yes` when the change widens or narrows the accept set or the public surface. `check-changeset-no-major` holds `yes (narrowing)` beside `narrowed` as coherent, `record-recognisers` maps it to the narrowing face, and the #31224 changeset for `flow-node-unreachable` carries the same line for the same shape. The claim said "the dev measures and reports", so the two do not conflict; the seat may amend the claim to match.
- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` with `minor` on `@objectstack/lint` is right.** A flow an author could save live, publish and build is now refused: "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`", and a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. `@objectstack/lint` is the only package whose source moves; the other eight files are tests. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two lines. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.
- The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, Before / Now, and what an author does.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Fixture edits outside the claimed surface: accepted.** The claim says to stop on breach and explain; the dev explained, and each edit is a consequence of the narrowing. See ④ for each file.
- **ADR-0087 upgrade-guide entry: not owed by the gate; escalated to the seat as a follow-up, not a blocker.** The claim asked for an entry "if the gates require one". `check-adr-0087-registration` asks a breaking changeset for a written disposition, and refuses `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` only when the body carries a FROM → TO rewrite it can read (an arrow, or a framed table). This body has neither, so the green is a pass by the gate's rule as written. It is also true that the body does tell the author what to write ("add a node with `type: 'start'`"), in prose the detector does not read; the ADR's own addendum names that limit. So the green proves the question was answered in writing, not that no guide entry would help. The precedents point both ways: `flow-node-unreachable` (#31224), the nearest sibling, took the same disposition and landed; `picklist-binding-unknown-refused` registered a semantic entry for a refusal with no mechanical rewrite. An entry would live in `packages/spec/src/migrations/`, which the claim bars. Recommendation: one follow-up card for the spec lane to decide both flow rules together.
- **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/automation.json`, recipe step `qa_no_start_node`: escalated.** It expects `2xx` from `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/qa_no_start_node` and says of #32289: "once it lands, re-read it and re-point this step". This PR is that landing and leaves the step. The dev disclosed it. See ④ nit 2.
- **#32288** owns the trigger tables in `content/docs`. I re-read `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` L2625 and L2630: both stay true after this PR (a flow stored before it is still not armed and reads `registration: refused`).
- The dev raised no `open_questions` entry beyond these.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes an existing refusal real earlier; it takes no declared capability away.** The published spec on `main` never declared that a flow may run without a start node: `FlowSchema` is silent, every run begins at the first top-level node whose `type === 'start'` (`engine.ts` L7205), and since #32273 the engine refuses to register the shape. The live save stored a flow that could never run and answered `200`. The rule moves the refusal to the door where the author is, keeps the mid-edit draft, and adds nothing the engine does not already hold. Placing it in lint rather than the parse is right for the reason the sibling rule gives: the parse runs on drafts.

**The wiring is proved at both levels.** `protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts`: the new `CASES` row runs the file's parametrised case (the draft saves, reads `valid: false` with the rule in `_diagnostics`, and the per-item publish answers `422 INVALID_METADATA`), and a new case pins the live save refused with nothing stored. `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts` pins the same on a real kernel.

**`rule-explanations.ts`.** The false sentence is corrected: the dangling-edge half stays (the parse does refuse that), and the start-less half now says "the parse accepts it, and `flow-start-node-missing` names it". The new entry matches the rule: zero start nodes only, top-level only, extra start nodes left to `flow-node-unreachable`, draft kept, live save and publish refused. "Would be refused with `FLOW_NO_START_NODE`" is conditional and agrees with the engine's own note that the exit is defensive.

**Fixture edits, file by file. None hides a behaviour change or weakens a pin.**
- `protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts`, the two `automation-flow-*` tests, `meta-managed-content-seal.test.ts`, `meta-overlay-read-your-writes.test.ts`: `nodes: []` becomes a lone start node on a body the test saves live. None of them asserts on the node list; each pins something else (override gate, package address, seal, read-your-writes). The added top-of-file imports only pay a lazy load at collection.
- `protocol.save-flow-canonicalization.test.ts`: `wiredFromStart` appends the start node last, so `nodes[0]` and every asserted index name the same node. The stub canonicalizer now keeps `nodes.slice(1)` where it rebuilt the list from `nodes[0]` alone; that is needed for the start node to survive and does not change what the stub converts. One assertion moves from `['n0', 'n1']` to `['n0', 'n1', 'start']`, which is the fixture, not the behaviour.
- **Commit `2ff43342`, the TS2353 fix: sound on reading, not yet confirmed by CI.** The earlier signature took an array of `{ id: string }`, which made the fresh object literals at L62 and L443 fail the excess-property check. The helper is now generic, `N extends { id: string }` with `nodes: N[]`, and infers `N` from the literal, so the check no longer applies and the constraint still requires `id: string`. `flowOf` tightens from `unknown[]` to an array of `{ id: string }` and drops a cast; its callers pass call results, not fresh literals. Nothing is loosened. `Type Check · workspace` was in progress when read, so this is my reading of the code and not a gate verdict.
- `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts`: the one rewritten case is the intended behaviour change, stated in its title. It pinned "a `status: 'draft'` flow saved LIVE stores, and the read says refused"; it now pins the live save refused with `flow-start-node-missing` and nothing registered, then a `mode: 'draft'` save stored with the finding. The read of a stored start-less row as `registration: refused` is still pinned by the case above it, which seeds the row.

**Findings.** No must-fix. No should-fix.

- **nit 1 — changeset body.** It does not say what happens to rows stored before this release: a live re-save of an already-stored start-less flow is refused until it gains a start node (no stored-row baseline, unlike the picklist precedent's "a binding the object already holds is not judged again"); a start-less draft stored earlier is judged when it is published, and blocks its package publish; delete, draft save and `os migrate meta --stored` are not judged. The PR body's "stored rows are not affected" is true only of a row nobody saves again. One sentence in the changeset would close it.
- **nit 2 — QA recipe.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/automation.json` step `qa_no_start_node` now expects a `2xx` that answers `422`. Re-point it in this PR if that file is a prose face here, or file the follow-up before landing.
- **nit 3 — stale docblock in a touched test.** `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts`, the block above the start-less `describe`: "Save: the metadata save door still keeps a start-less body (it does not run the registration checks), and the mutation sync records the same refusal." The case below it now pins the opposite for a live save. A fix moves the head, so leave it as an accepted deviation or fold it into the follow-up.
- **nit 4 — PR body.** It names `4c099270` as the final head and round 2 as running; the head is `80e82e18`, with `2ff43342` and a merge of `main` after it.
- **nit 5 — ADR-0087.** The follow-up card recommended in ③.
